author: Asp-irin
body:
## Current Problem 

The status timeline endpoint runs an inefficient query:

```sql
FROM time_series
LEFT JOIN filtered_status_history
  ON created_ts >= ts - interval '3 days'
  AND created_ts < ts
```

**What happens:**
- Loads 33,389 history rows
- Checks each row against 11 timeline buckets
- Keeps matches, discards the rest

**The waste:**
- Total comparisons: 11 × 33,389 = 367,279
- Rows discarded: 333,890 (91% wasted)
- Execution time: **64.3 ms**

---
**Note**: As i don't have direct data access i generated 200k rows randomly using a query to get some relevant results. Maintainers are requested to run the queries against the DB may be staging or prod depending on the input data we have. If there is any test DB with good amount of data I am happy to work on it to share correct metrics!

---

## Why This Matters

As history rows grow, the query does more unnecessary work.

For groups with lots of status updates, this slows down timeline reports.

The query loads all rows first, then filters. It should fetch only relevant rows per bucket instead.

---

## The Solution

**Instead of:** Get all rows, then check them against buckets

**Do this:** For each bucket, get only rows that belong to it

**Improved query:**
```sql
FROM ranges AS r
LEFT JOIN LATERAL (
  SELECT status, version, instance_id
  FROM instance_status_history
  WHERE group_id = $1
    AND created_ts >= r.from_ts
    AND created_ts < r.ts
) AS ish ON true
```

**Results:**
- Execution time: **20.5 ms** (3.1x faster)
- Comparisons: ~30-50K instead of 367K
- Minimal wasted work

---

## Implementation Steps

### Step 1: Add Index
```sql
CREATE INDEX ON instance_status_history (group_id, created_ts);
```

### Step 2: Rewrite Query
Use LATERAL join to filter per-bucket instead of loading all rows at once.

---

## Performance Comparison

| Metric | Current | Improved |
|---|---|---|
| Execution time | 64.3 ms | 20.5 ms |
| Speed improvement | Baseline | **3.1x faster** |
| Rows checked | 367K | 30-50K |
| Wasted comparisons | 333K (91%) | Minimal |

---

## Validation Needed

Before a PR is raised I would like maintainers to confirm this:

1. Run EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS) on both queries with real production data
2. Verify both queries return identical results
3. Test different time ranges (1h, 1d, 7d, 30d)
4. Check index size and write overhead on `instance_status_history`
5. Confirm performance improvement on live data

---

## What Gets Changed

- New index on `(group_id, created_ts)`
- Query rewrite using LATERAL join
- Unit/integration tests for regression prevention

---

## Summary

Move filtering from after-the-join to before-the-join by using LATERAL with targeted index scans per bucket instead of checking all rows against all buckets.


## Proof of Work

[Proposed-Query-Explain-Report](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31139178/after-analyse-report.txt)
[Existing-Query-Explain-Report](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31139177/existing-analyse-buffer-report.txt)
title: [RFE] Optimize Group Status Timeline query performance

author: aeron-gh
body:
`instance_application` and `instance_status_history` carry indexes that are fully covered by other indexes on the same table. Five of the six sit on the two tables Nebraska writes to most, `instance_application` on every Omaha check-in and `instance_status_history` on every status change, so the cost scales with fleet size.

## What is redundant

One is an exact duplicate of a primary key. Migration 0011 added `instance_application_instance_id_application_id_idx` on `(instance_id, application_id)`, but that is exactly the primary key declared in 0001. Postgres already maintains a unique index for the key, so this is a second copy of the same B-tree. At 200k rows both measure 15 MB.

The other five are leading prefixes of wider indexes, so the wider index can serve the same predicates:

| table | redundant index | columns | covered by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| instance_application | `instance_application_instance_id_application_id_idx` | instance_id, application_id | `instance_application_pkey`, identical |
| instance_application | `instance_application_instance_id_idx` | instance_id | `instance_application_pkey` |
| instance_application | `instance_application_group_id_idx` | group_id | `instance_application_group_id_last_check_for_updates_instan_idx` |
| instance_status_history | `instance_status_history_instance_id_idx` | instance_id | `instance_status_history_instance_id_status_created_ts_idx` |
| instance_status_history | `instance_status_history_group_id_idx` | group_id | `instance_status_history_group_id_status_created_ts_idx` |
| channel_package_floors | `idx_channel_package_floors_channel` | channel_id | `channel_package_floors_pkey` |

The four single column indexes come from `create index on <table> (<col>)` in 0001, so Postgres auto-named them. Most were overtaken later, when the wider indexes arrived in 0013, 0016 and 0020. `instance_application_instance_id_idx` is the exception: the primary key that covers it is declared on line 119 of 0001 and the index is created on line 122 of the same file, so it has been redundant since the first migration.

Both of the following are reproducible on any database with all 23 migrations applied. The first finds prefix overlaps, the second finds exact duplicates, which the first cannot see because it only considers strictly wider indexes:

```sql
with idx as (
  select t.relname as tbl, i.relname as idx,
         ix.indisprimary as is_pk, ix.indisunique as is_uniq,
         array_agg(a.attname order by k.ord) as cols
  from pg_index ix
  join pg_class i on i.oid = ix.indexrelid
  join pg_class t on t.oid = ix.indrelid
  join pg_namespace n on n.oid = t.relnamespace
  join lateral unnest(ix.indkey) with ordinality as k(attnum, ord) on true
  join pg_attribute a on a.attrelid = t.oid and a.attnum = k.attnum
  where n.nspname = 'public' and t.relkind = 'r'
  group by 1,2,3,4
)
select a.tbl, a.idx as redundant, b.idx as covered_by
from idx a join idx b
  on a.tbl = b.tbl and a.idx <> b.idx
 and array_length(a.cols,1) < array_length(b.cols,1)
 and b.cols[1:array_length(a.cols,1)] = a.cols
where not a.is_pk and not a.is_uniq;
```

```sql
with idx as (
  select t.relname as tbl, i.relname as idx,
         array_to_string(array_agg(a.attname order by k.ord), ',') as cols
  from pg_index ix
  join pg_class i on i.oid = ix.indexrelid
  join pg_class t on t.oid = ix.indrelid
  join pg_namespace n on n.oid = t.relnamespace
  join lateral unnest(ix.indkey) with ordinality as k(attnum, ord) on true
  join pg_attribute a on a.attrelid = t.oid and a.attnum = k.attnum
  where n.nspname = 'public' and t.relkind = 'r'
  group by 1,2
)
select tbl, cols, array_to_string(array_agg(idx), ' | ') as duplicates
from idx group by 1,2 having count(*) > 1;
```

## Measured cost

PostgreSQL 17, 200k instances, one `instance_application` row each, then a full update pass to simulate a fleet wide check-in round.

Index footprint on the two hot tables, which does not depend on run order:

| | current | six dropped |
| --- | --- | --- |
| total index bytes | 133 MB | 95 MB |

That is 38 MB, about 29%, at 200k instances.

For timings I ran the workload in both orders, because a single ordering is contaminated by cache warm up. `instance` has no index change in either configuration, so it acts as a control:

| workload | run 1, current first | run 2, dropped first |
| --- | --- | --- |
| insert into `instance` (control) | dropped 45% faster | dropped 30% **slower** |
| insert into `instance_application` | dropped 44% faster | dropped 45% faster |
| update `instance_application` | dropped 68% faster | dropped 57% faster |
| insert into `instance_status_history` | dropped 27% faster | dropped 28% faster |

The control flips sign between the two orders, which is what warm up should do. The three affected workloads keep both their sign and roughly their magnitude regardless of order, so the improvement is attributable to the indexes rather than to ordering. Absolute times vary a lot between runs on my machine, so the percentages are the meaningful part.

## Foreign keys still covered

`instance_status_history.instance_id` and `.group_id`, and `instance_application.group_id`, are all referencing columns with `on delete cascade` or `on delete set null`. Those need an index to avoid a sequential scan when the parent row goes away. Every one of them is still covered after the drops, by `(instance_id, status, created_ts)`, `(group_id, status, created_ts)`, the primary key, and `(group_id, last_check_for_updates, instance_id)` respectively.

## Caveat

A narrower index is smaller than the wide one that covers it, so in principle it can win on cache residency for a very hot lookup. I have not found a query where that applies here, and it does not apply at all to the exact duplicate of the primary key, but it is worth a maintainer's eye rather than being assumed away.

## Proposal

Add a migration that drops these six, in the same shape as the existing cleanups in 0012 and 0017, with the `create index` statements in the Down section so it is reversible.

Happy to open the PR if this looks right. I can also split the exact duplicate of the primary key into its own change if you would rather land the unambiguous part first.
title: Redundant indexes on instance_application and instance_status_history

author: Moustafa-Moustafa
body:
# feat: add the opt-in instance mode for distributed deployments

The distributed topology in RFC #1375 introduces one control node that accepts admin writes, and N edge nodes that serve Omaha update checks. #1575 built the database half of that, two group roles carrying different table privileges, but nothing chose between them. This adds the switch that chooses.

`NEBRASKA_INSTANCE_MODE`, also settable with `--instance-mode`, places a node as `single`, `control` or `edge`. An edge is granted `nebraska_runtime_<database>` refuses the admin endpoints with 403, and will not start with `--enable-syncer`, since the syncer creates packages and moves channels. `control` and `edge` both require `NEBRASKA_MIGRATIONS_DB_URL` to name a different user than `NEBRASKA_DB_URL`, because without that separation there is no database boundary to enforce.

Which endpoints are admin is declared in `api/spec.yaml` as an `x-nebraska-node-role` on every one of the existing operations, and the guard builds its deny set from the embedded spec at startup. An operation carrying no extension makes the server refuse to start and names the operation, so an endpoint added without deciding where it runs cannot ship. A test asserts the classification matches the routes actually registered on the router, so the spec cannot drift from the server either.

The HTTP guard is the second line of defense, not the only one. Without it an edge already fails an admin write at the database with `permission denied for table application`; the guard turns that 500 into a 403 that explains itself. Both layers are exercised in the live validation below.

An edge also needs to stop updates for its own fleet without changing the group default the control node replicates out. `DELETE /api/apps/{appIDorProductID}/groups/{groupID}/updates_override` clears the node-local brake and nothing else. A single-instance deployment has one updates-enabled switch and no local override, so it answers 501 there.

A follow-up splits `pkg/handler` into admin and runtime halves, where the single-mode brake clear in `UpdateGroup` moves behind a narrow injected interface rather than handing the admin handler the runtime service.

Deployments that do not set `NEBRASKA_INSTANCE_MODE` are untouched. The guard is never registered, none of the validation this adds can fire, and the serving role is chosen exactly as before.

Refs: #1375

## How to use

No new behavior is introduced for anyone who does not set `NEBRASKA_INSTANCE_MODE`, so the first thing to validate is that a single-instance deployment is not impacted at all. Left unset, it is `single`, and startup, grants and every endpoint behave as they do today.

To exercise the distributed path, give each node its own serving login and validate that the control node accepts admin writes and is granted the admin role while the edge node is granted the runtime role instead, and refuses the admin surface, and its Omaha update checks keep working, and the instances that check in against it are recorded in its own database.

## Testing done

```console
$ cd backend
$ make code-checks
go build ./...
./tools/check_pkg_test.sh
NEBRASKA_SKIP_TESTS=1 go test ./... >/dev/null
./tools/golangci-lint run --fix
0 issues.
go mod tidy
```

```console
$ make check-backend-with-container
ok  github.com/flatcar/nebraska/backend/pkg/api                    29.478s
ok  github.com/flatcar/nebraska/backend/pkg/api/admin              0.274s
ok  github.com/flatcar/nebraska/backend/pkg/api/runtime            3.001s
ok  github.com/flatcar/nebraska/backend/pkg/auth                   0.006s
ok  github.com/flatcar/nebraska/backend/pkg/config                 0.010s
ok  github.com/flatcar/nebraska/backend/pkg/middleware             0.071s
ok  github.com/flatcar/nebraska/backend/pkg/omaha                  4.536s
ok  github.com/flatcar/nebraska/backend/pkg/random                 0.004s
ok  github.com/flatcar/nebraska/backend/pkg/sessions               0.006s
ok  github.com/flatcar/nebraska/backend/pkg/sessions/memcache      0.006s
ok  github.com/flatcar/nebraska/backend/pkg/sessions/memcache/gob  0.006s
ok  github.com/flatcar/nebraska/backend/pkg/syncer                 6.389s
ok  github.com/flatcar/nebraska/backend/test/api                   23.201s
ok  github.com/flatcar/nebraska/backend/test/auth/oidc             3.845s
```

A local end-to-end script covering the full admin CRUD and Omaha surface passes identically against this branch and against unmodified `main`, confirming the single-instance path is unchanged.

Two Nebraska processes were then run against one Postgres, each with its own database and serving login, and checked end to end: the control node is granted the admin role and the edge the runtime role; all 14 admin operations answer 403 on the edge with a stable error code; reads, `/health`, `/config`, `/metrics` and Omaha still answer 200 on the edge; an instance that checks in against the edge is recorded in the edge database and is absent from the control database; the local brake clear works on the edge and answers 501 on a single-instance node; and the invalid configurations are each refused at startup.

author: Moustafa-Moustafa
body:
# feat(db): allow a provider to supply the database password

Nebraska takes the database password from `NEBRASKA_DB_URL`. That string is fixed for the life of the process, so a deployment whose credential expires, such as an OAuth token from a cloud identity provider, has no in-process way to supply a new one: the first connection attempted after expiry fails, and so does every one after that.

`DBPasswordProvider` is an optional hook consulted before each physical connection. When one is installed the handle is opened through pgx's `BeforeConnect` callback, which runs for every new connection and receives a fresh copy of the connection config, so the provider can return a credential renewed since startup. How that credential is obtained is not Nebraska's concern, and no cloud SDK is added; `go.mod` is unchanged.

The callback runs before pgx applies `connect_timeout`, so the provider call is bounded by that same timeout. A provider that never answers fails the connection instead of holding up every one the pool is trying to open.

The provider is given the user the connection authenticates as, so a single provider can serve connections made as different roles. That is what a deployment needs if it ever runs migrations under a separate role, as #1575 proposes.

Deployments that install no provider are untouched. The plain `sqlx.Open` path runs exactly as before and the password keeps coming from `NEBRASKA_DB_URL`.

## How to use

No new behavior is introduced for anyone who does not install a provider, so the first thing to validate is that an existing deployment is not impacted at all.

To use it, implement the interface and install it in `cmd/nebraska/main.go` before the database is created:

```go
type tokenProvider struct{}

func (tokenProvider) DBPassword(ctx context.Context, user string) (string, error) {
    // fetch a short-lived credential for this role, e.g. a cloud IAM token
    return fetchToken(ctx, user)
}
```

```diff
 func main() {
     conf, err := config.Parse()
     ...
+	db.SetDBPasswordProvider(tokenProvider{})
+
     if conf.RollbackDBTo != "" {
         db, err := db.New()
```

It goes above the `RollbackDBTo` branch so it covers both connections `main` can open, the down-migration one and `db.NewWithMigrations()`.

The password in `NEBRASKA_DB_URL` is then ignored; the user, host and database in it are still used.

The same shape is used by [netdata](https://github.com/netdata/netdata/blob/master/src/go/plugin/go.d/collector/postgres/collect.go) for Azure Entra ID and [bytebase](https://github.com/bytebase/bytebase/blob/main/backend/store/dbauth/aws.go) for AWS RDS IAM.


## Testing done

```console
$ cd backend
$ make code-checks
go build ./...
./tools/check_pkg_test.sh
NEBRASKA_SKIP_TESTS=1 go test ./... >/dev/null
./tools/golangci-lint run --fix
0 issues.
go mod tidy
```

```console
$ make check-backend-with-container
ok  github.com/flatcar/nebraska/backend/pkg/api             22.504s
ok  github.com/flatcar/nebraska/backend/pkg/api/admin        0.248s
ok  github.com/flatcar/nebraska/backend/pkg/api/runtime      2.681s
ok  github.com/flatcar/nebraska/backend/pkg/auth             0.009s
ok  github.com/flatcar/nebraska/backend/pkg/middleware       0.008s
ok  github.com/flatcar/nebraska/backend/pkg/omaha            3.947s
ok  github.com/flatcar/nebraska/backend/pkg/random           0.003s
ok  github.com/flatcar/nebraska/backend/pkg/sessions         0.006s
ok  github.com/flatcar/nebraska/backend/pkg/sessions/memcache      0.005s
ok  github.com/flatcar/nebraska/backend/pkg/sessions/memcache/gob  0.005s

ok  github.com/flatcar/nebraska/backend/test/api            21.491s

Three tests cover the new path: that the provider is consulted for every connection and a rotated credential is picked up, that a provider error fails the connection, and that without a provider the URL password is still used.

author: pinankshah8-Aa
body:
Fixes #1553

## Why

`RegisterEvent` could store a malformed `previousVersion` even though instance registration already validates version strings. I reproduced this on current `main` with Nebraska's real API test harness and PostgreSQL: after putting an instance into an update-in-progress state, `RegisterEvent(..., "not-a-version", ...)` returned `nil`.

## What changed

- Validate non-empty, non-`0.0.0.0` `previousVersion` values with the existing `dbreads.IsValidSemver()` helper.
- Return the existing `types.ErrInvalidSemver` before inserting the event when validation fails.
- Preserve the existing Flatcar-specific empty / `0.0.0.0` behavior.
- Add a regression case to `TestRegisterEvent_InvalidParams` that exercises `RegisterEvent` itself.

## Validation

- `go test -p 1 ./pkg/api/... -count=1` against PostgreSQL 17 — passed.
- `go build ./...` — passed.
- `./tools/check_pkg_test.sh` — passed.
- `NEBRASKA_SKIP_TESTS=1 go test ./...` — passed.
- `golangci-lint v2.12.2 run` — 0 issues.
- `git diff --check` — passed.
- `gofmt -d` on both changed Go files — no diff.

## AI assistance

I used ChatGPT to assist with codebase exploration, test planning, and review. I personally reproduced the bug, reviewed and understand every change, and ran the validation above myself.
title: fix(api): validate event previous version

author: KartikSuryavanshi
body:
Closes #374

## Summary

Makes Nebraska's development tooling work on macOS, which ships bash 3.2 and BSD utilities by default.

## Changes

- **`backend/tools/check_pkg_test.sh`** — replaced `mapfile` (bash 4+) with a `while read` loop, which works on the bash 3.2 shipped with macOS. Verified by running the script under `/bin/bash` (3.2.57).
- **`backend/tools/setup_local_db.sh`** and **`backend/tools/run-all.sh`** — replaced the GNU `getopt --longoptions` calls with portable argument parsing that also supports the `--opt=value` form used by `run-all.sh`. Verified under `/bin/bash` (3.2): short, long, and `=` forms parse; invalid and missing arguments produce clean errors.
- **`backend/Makefile`** — only passes `-extldflags "-static"` on non-macOS platforms. On macOS the system linker (`clang`) does not support static linking and the build fails with `ld: library 'crt0.o' not found`. Verified: `make -C backend build` now produces `backend/bin/nebraska` (Mach-O) on macOS; Linux container builds keep the flag.
- **`docs/development-macos.md`** — new macOS development guide, linked from the README's Development section.
- **`CHANGELOG.md`** — changelog entry.

## Verification

- All three scripts pass `bash -n` and run correctly under `/bin/bash` 3.2.
- `make -C backend build` succeeds on macOS (previously failed at link time).
- `NEBRASKA_SKIP_TESTS=1 go test -p 1 ./...` passes.
- Full test suite (DB-backed) requires Docker, so it runs in CI.
title: fix(dev): enable development on macOS

author: amanmaurya92
body:
### Fix #1578: Refactor Instances list component to use URL as single source of truth for state

This PR refactors the `Instances/List.tsx` component to eliminate redundant local React state hooks (`useState`) for pagination, rows per page, sorting order, and filtering. Previously, the component maintained its own state in parallel with the browser's URL, which occasionally caused desynchronization and unnecessary re-renders. 

By deriving the component's state directly from `location.search` via `URLSearchParams` on every render, the URL is now the single source of truth. The massive `handleInstanceFetch` function and `fetchFiltersFromURL` callbacks have been stripped down into a streamlined `useEffect` hook that listens directly to URL changes. This ensures that when users navigate history, share URLs, or manually interact with the Instances table, the state and the UI remain perfectly perfectly in sync.

## How to use

1. Run the backend and frontend development servers.
2. Navigate to an Application's group instance list.
3. Change the page or adjust the rows per page on the Instances table—verify the URL updates correctly and the new data loads.
4. Apply the Status or Version filters, or search for instances—verify the URL and table reflect the changes.
5. Click the browser's "Back" and "Forward" buttons—verify the component correctly reverts to the previous page/filter state without desynchronization.

## Testing done

Executed the frontend linters, TypeScript compiler, and unit test suite successfully. The unit tests verify that the component mounts and behaves properly after the refactor.

Commands run:
```bash
npm run lint
npm run test
```

author: ervcz
body:
Forward ports the two 4.0.0 security fixes onto `main`. Both are already released and described in GHSA-8535-v9q5-f7qp, which is public.

OIDC access tokens were verified for signature, issuer and expiry but not audience, so a token the provider issued for any other application in the same realm was accepted. `--oidc-audience` is now required in OIDC mode and checked against the `aud` claim, and tokens that identify themselves as ID tokens are rejected. This is a breaking change for OIDC deployments, see the migration guide. The test realm fixture gains an audience mapper, which the end to end tests need in order to mint tokens carrying `aud: nebraska-api`.

The `groupID` path parameter of the group version timeline endpoint was interpolated into three SQL statements. All three now bind it as a query parameter, and the endpoint declares `groupID` as a UUID in the OpenAPI spec so malformed values are rejected before reaching the database.

The changelog commits move the 4.0.0 entries out of `[Unreleased]` into a released 4.0.0 section, so `main`'s record of 4.0.0 matches the release branch.

Two unrelated tidy-ups ride along. `config.caFile` returns to the chart: it was dropped so chart 3.0.0, which declares appVersion 4.0.0, would not offer a value the 4.0.0 image rejects, and that chart is now published. The `--oidc-roles-path` help said the roles array is in the id token when `Authorize` reads it from the access token.

No UserInfo commit here, `main` already has that feature.
title: fix(auth): validate OIDC access token audience

author: riyacore404
body:
# application_instances_per_channel metric undercounts/miscounts instances

The `nebraska_application_instances_per_channel` gauge had three bugs relative
to the rest of the codebase:

1. **Dead instances counted forever** — the query never filtered on
   `last_check_for_updates`, so instances that stopped checking in stayed in
   the metric indefinitely instead of aging out like every other
   activity-based query (`GetApp`, `GetApps`, `GetInstances`, etc).
2. **Instances with no channel silently dropped** — the query used comma
   joins across `groups`/`channel`, so any instance whose group had no
   channel assigned (`groups.channel_id` can be NULL) disappeared from the
   metric entirely rather than being counted.
3. **amd64/arm64 channels merged into one series** — the query grouped only
   by channel name, so two channels sharing a name across architectures
   (e.g. "stable" for amd64 and arm64) were folded into a single row.

This fixes all three: adds the same freshness filter used elsewhere, switches
to `LEFT JOIN` for groups/channel so channel-less instances land in an
explicit "no channel" bucket instead of vanishing, and adds `arch` to the
grouping so per-architecture counts are reported separately.

Fixes #1562

## How to use

No config or API changes — the fix is internal to how
`GetAppInstancesPerChannelMetrics` computes the `application_instances_per_channel`
Prometheus gauge. Reviewers can validate by scraping `/metrics` on a
Nebraska instance with some inactive instances and/or a channel-less group
and confirming the counts now match what's shown in the instances UI.

author: aeron-gh
body:
Refs: #1131

## What

Build the updater against the backend in the checkout instead of the published pseudo-version pinned in `updater/go.mod`, and fix the workflow path filters so backend changes reach the updater job at all.

- `updater/updater_test.go`: adapt to the `pkg/api` admin and runtime split from #1434 and #1498, and realign the backend pin past it, since the current pin predates the split and the two no longer build together
- `.github/workflows/updater.yml`: trigger on `backend/**`, and run `go work init ./backend ./updater` before the tests
- `.github/workflows/backend.yml`: drop the `updaters/**` filter. The directory is `updater/`, so it never matched, and nothing under `backend/` imports the updater, so backend CI has no reason to run on updater changes. Repairing the typo would only have added CI runs that cannot fail for a related reason
- `go.work` and `go.work.sum` are gitignored, with the command in the ignore comment so it is discoverable

## Why

`updater/updater_test.go` is the only thing in the updater that depends on the backend, and it compiles against the pin rather than the working tree. A backend change therefore cannot break the updater's tests in the PR that causes it, which is the "two changes for each one that we make" in #1131.

@ervcz set out the shape of the fix on the issue: use a `replace` for local development, keep it out of the tree, and refresh the outdated pin. This PR follows that, with a Go workspace as the mechanism so CI can use it too. `go.work` is not part of the published module, so it cannot reach consumers. A committed `replace` would not reach them either, since Go ignores `replace` outside the main module, but it would then sit in the published `go.mod` doing nothing while hiding the pin from every local build. The workspace keeps that separation explicit.

The drift this exposes is recurring. #1414 refreshed the pin to the pgx v5 merge and ported `updateinfo.go` to the new `go-omaha` `Manifests` field, but since that refresh the `pkg/api` split has drifted the two modules apart again. On `main` today:

```
$ go work init ./backend ./updater && go vet ./updater/...
updater\updater_test.go:31:29: cannot use api (variable of type *api.API) as *"github.com/flatcar/nebraska/backend/pkg/api/runtime".Service value in argument to omaha.NewHandler
updater\updater_test.go:121:29: apiInstance.AddPackage undefined (type *api.API has no field or method AddPackage)
updater\updater_test.go:124:20: apiInstance.UpdateChannel undefined (type *api.API has no field or method UpdateChannel)
updater\updater_test.go:173:24: cnf.api.AddTeam undefined (type *api.API has no field or method AddTeam)
updater\updater_test.go:175:23: cnf.api.AddApp undefined (type *api.API has no field or method AddApp)
updater\updater_test.go:177:23: cnf.api.AddPackage undefined (type *api.API has no field or method AddPackage)
updater\updater_test.go:179:27: cnf.api.AddChannel undefined (type *api.API has no field or method AddChannel)
updater\updater_test.go:181:25: cnf.api.AddGroup undefined (type *api.API has no field or method AddGroup)
```

None of that is covered by CI today. The first commit fixes the current break, the second makes it CI's job to catch the next one in the PR that causes it.

## Trade-offs

These are the costs of the approach, worth weighing before it lands:

- CI now exercises the working tree rather than the pinned pseudo-version, so the pin could go stale without anything failing. The impact is limited because the backend is a test-only dependency of the updater and consumers of the library never build it, but the pin does need its own upkeep.
- A workspace applies MVS across both modules, so the updater resolves to the backend's dependency versions. That is real coupling rather than a free win: the updater picks up backend dependency bumps whether or not it needs them.
- I have not verified how the existing `gomod` Dependabot entry for `/updater` behaves with a workspace in CI. It is untouched here and should be unaffected, since `go.work` is generated at job time and never committed, but I have not tested that.

## Rebase note

Rebased onto current `main`. #1414 landed the pin refresh to pgx v5, the `go` 1.25 raise and the `updateinfo.go` port to `Manifests`, so this PR no longer carries any of that and `updateinfo.go` is untouched here. The manifest selection question from the previous revision, first entry versus last, was settled by #1414 on `Manifests[0]`, so this PR takes no position on it and any revisit belongs with the multi step update work in #1166.

Rebased again after #1552 made the domain types public and #1556 reworked the shared connection, which broke the updater tests against the in-tree backend a third time. The first commit absorbs that adaptation and moves the pin to current `main`.

## Testing

With the workspace in place, against the current tree, `go vet ./updater/...` and `go build ./updater/...` pass:

```
$ go work init ./backend ./updater
$ go vet ./updater/...
$ go build ./updater/...
```

And the published pin still builds on its own, without a workspace:

```
$ GOWORK=off go vet ./...   # in updater/
```

The full updater suite against PostgreSQL 17 last ran on the previous revision of this branch. The only test change since is the adaptation to the split, and the workspace CI arrangement this PR adds runs exactly that suite.

## Follow-up

I originally documented the workspace in `CONTRIBUTING.md`, but dropped it when rebasing onto #1440, which moved Nebraska development guidance to the [development guide](https://www.flatcar.org/docs/latest/updates-releases/nebraska/development/). Happy to send it there instead if you think it is worth documenting.

Tagging backend releases (`backend/v0.1.0`) so Dependabot can bump the updater automatically needs a maintainer to push tags, so it is not something this PR can do. With the workspace in place the pin no longer blocks development, so it only affects keeping the published module graph current.
title: build(updater): track backend dependency via Go workspace

author: aeron-gh
body:
Refs: #1008

## What

Return 409 instead of 500 when creating a package that already exists, and make the syncer treat that same condition as benign.

- `pkg/api/types/errors.go`: a new `ErrDuplicatePackage` sentinel, defined next to the existing ones
- `pkg/api/admin/packages.go`: detect the unique constraint violation on the package insert and return the sentinel
- `pkg/handler/packages.go`: map it to 409, in the same `switch err` shape already used for the other client errors in this file
- `api/spec.yaml` and the regenerated `spec.gen.go`: document the 409 on `createPackage`
- `pkg/syncer/syncer.go`: on a duplicate, adopt the existing package instead of failing the channel sync

## Why

Uploading a package that already exists returned a 500, because `CreatePackage` returned a blanket `StatusInternalServerError` for anything `AddPackage` failed on and nothing in `pkg/` classified the Postgres unique violation. A client mistake looked like a server fault, which is what #1008 describes.

Detection sits next to the insert in the admin service rather than in the handler, so `pkg/handler` does not need to know Postgres error codes. That matches how `ErrInvalidPackage` and `ErrArchMismatch` are already surfaced. It is scoped to the `package` insert specifically, since `addPackage` also writes `package_channel_blacklist`, whose primary key raises the same SQLSTATE, and a conflict there is not a duplicate package.

The handler returns a fixed message rather than the underlying error. The sentinel text and the SQLSTATE are useful in logs, not in a response body.

## The syncer

@ervcz pointed out on the issue that the syncer reaches the same insert through `AddPackageWithMetadata`, and asked what happens to already downloaded files when that insert fails.

`getOrCreatePackage` already checks `GetPackageByVersionAndArch` for the same app, version and arch triple the constraint covers, so the syncer only reaches the insert when the package is genuinely absent. A duplicate therefore means either a race with another writer, or a transient failure on that read, since any error on that read falls through to `createPackage`.

That second question mattered more than I expected. With `hostPackages` enabled the payload filename is derived from arch and version, and the extra file names from arch, version and the original name, so a syncer-created row for that version already points at exactly the paths just written. The existing cleanup on insert failure removes them, so a duplicate deleted the payloads of the package that already existed while its row kept advertising them. That is the behaviour on main today, independent of this change.

The duplicate branch therefore skips the cleanup, logs at info since the syncer is an unattended background process, and returns the existing package so the channel sync carries on. If that lookup itself fails it logs a warning and returns the original error rather than a misleading one.

## Rebase note

Rebased over the `pkg/api` write surface split (#1434, #1498). The detection moved with `addPackage` into `pkg/api/admin`. The unit tests moved to the new `pkg/api/admin/packages_test.go`.

Rebased again over #1552 and #1556. The domain types are public now, so the sentinel lives in `pkg/api/types/errors.go` and the handler and syncer reference `types.ErrDuplicatePackage` directly, matching how `types.ErrArchMismatch` is handled since that refactor. No re-export in `pkg/api` anymore, upstream dropped that pattern.

## Testing

Added:

- `TestAddPackageDuplicate`, covering `AddPackage`, `AddPackageWithMetadata`, and that a different arch or version is not a duplicate
- `TestAddPackageBlacklistConflictIsNotDuplicate`, which pins the scoping down: a `package_channel_blacklist` primary key conflict raises the same SQLSTATE and must not surface as `ErrDuplicatePackage`
- `TestIsUniqueViolation`, a database free unit test of the classifier across bare, wrapped, foreign key, plain and nil errors
- `TestSyncer_CreatePackageDuplicate`, asserting the syncer returns the existing package
- `TestSyncer_CreatePackageDuplicateKeepsHostedFiles`, which serves a real payload over `httptest`, triggers the duplicate, and asserts the main payload and both extra files are still on disk with the right contents
- a `duplicate_conflict` case in `test/api/package_test.go`, asserting the endpoint returns 409 and that the body leaks neither the sentinel text nor the SQLSTATE

After the rebase, `go build ./...` and `go vet ./...` (which also typechecks the test files) pass, and rerunning `make codegen` with the pinned oapi-codegen v2.3.0 produces no diff.

The results below are from the previous revision of this branch, before the rebase onto the `pkg/api` split. The ported tests carry the same assertions in the new location, and CI runs the full suite:

```
ok  github.com/flatcar/nebraska/backend/pkg/api      131.778s
ok  github.com/flatcar/nebraska/backend/pkg/omaha     11.636s
ok  github.com/flatcar/nebraska/backend/pkg/syncer    16.195s
ok  github.com/flatcar/nebraska/backend/test/api       5.890s

--- PASS: TestAddPackageDuplicate
--- PASS: TestAddPackageBlacklistConflictIsNotDuplicate
--- PASS: TestIsUniqueViolation
--- PASS: TestSyncer_CreatePackageDuplicate
--- PASS: TestSyncer_CreatePackageDuplicateKeepsHostedFiles
--- PASS: TestCreatePackage/duplicate_conflict
```

`TestSyncer_CreatePackageDuplicateKeepsHostedFiles` is the one worth pointing at: it serves a real payload over `httptest`, triggers the duplicate, and asserts the main payload and both extra files are still on disk with the right contents.

## Note

Happy to split the syncer commit out if you would rather review the two separately, it is self contained.
title: fix(api): return 409 for duplicate package uploads

author: kartikangiras
body:
# Update the status code to return 409 Conflict instead of 500 when uploading a duplicate package

The PR fix is applied at every layer the insert touches: the shared addPackage path catches the postgres unique-violation code (SQLSTATE 23505) and returns a sentinel ErrPackageAlreadyExists error; the HTTP handler maps it to a 409 with a human-readable message; the syncer (unattended background process) gracefully falls back to the already-registered package instead of erroring out every sync tick. A subtle but important side-effect: when hostPackages is enabled and the syncer's insert hits a duplicate, downloaded payload files are now kept on disk instead of deleted, because those files use deterministic names that the already-registered DB row may reference, the old error path would have removed them and broken payload serving.
fixes #1008 

## How to use

1. Run the backend (with postgres).  
2. curl -X POST /api/apps/{appID}/packages with a valid package payload.  
3. curl -X POST /api/apps/{appID}/packages with the same appID, version and arch.  
4. The second call returns HTTP 409 with body nebraska: package already exists: appID, version , arch
5. Check the server log, it shows WRN addPackage package already exists instead of the previous ERR with the raw SQLSTATE 23505.

author: kartikangiras
body:
# Add edge case tests for multi step update floor packages

This PR adds comprehensive edge-case test coverage for the multi-step update (floor packages) feature. While the feature was implemented and tested for the happy path, several edge cases lacked test coverage: packages marked as floors being deleted, orphaned target packages, out-of-range floors, and syncer behavior when floor count exceeds the response limit.

Relates to #1172 
Five new tests ensure that:

Floor deletion is protected: packages marked as floors cannot be deleted until unmarked
Orphaned targets are handled gracefully: deleting a channel's target package (which is allowed) doesn't cause crashes; update requests fail with ErrNoPackageFound
Out-of-range floors are ignored: a floor mistakenly marked with a version higher than the target is excluded from all update paths, preventing instances from getting wedged on an unreachable prerequisite
Sequential progression works with per-query limits: regular clients step through all floors one by one, even when the floor count exceeds NEBRASKA_MAX_FLOORS_PER_RESPONSE
Syncer floor truncation is documented: a real gap where syncers receiving truncated floor lists are still granted to the full target is pinned down with a test that explains the limitation and will fail once it's fixed

Fixes #1441

On the instance details page, opening the rename dialog and hitting Cancel still triggered a refetch even though nothing was saved. Cancel calls `onHide()` with no argument, so `newInstance` comes through as `undefined`. The check was `newInstance !== null`, and since `undefined !== null` is true, `onInstanceUpdated()` ran anyway.

The fix changes that check to `newInstance !== undefined`. Cancel closes the dialog and stops there. Save still passes the updated instance back and refetches as before.

A test was added in `frontend/src/__tests__/Instances/Details.spec.tsx` covering both paths — cancel should not refetch, save should.

Pull the branch and open any instance details page. Click the menu, choose Rename, then Cancel without changing anything. The dialog should close and you should not see a fresh `GET` for that instance in the network tab.

To confirm save still works, open Rename again, change the alias, hit Save, and check that the page updates with the new name.

Run the unit tests with:

```
cd frontend
npx cross-env TEST_TZ=true npx vitest run src/__tests__/Instances/Details.spec.tsx
```

Both tests should pass.

Fixes: #1433

Deleting an app or group looked like it worked even when the server said no. The UI removed the item, showed nothing wrong, and a refresh brought it back. That happened because DELETE requests skipped the same error check as every other API call, and the store always cleared local state when the promise resolved.

This PR checks `response.ok` for DELETE in `API.doRequest` and adds error handling in `deleteApplication` and `deleteGroup` so the list only updates after a successful response. If the server returns 403 or 500 the item stays put and the user gets a generic error alert.

Pull the branch and run the frontend against a backend where you can trigger a failed delete. cd frontend
npx cross-env TEST_TZ=true npx vitest run src/__tests__/Api/api.spec.js src/__tests__/stores/ApplicationsStore.delete.spec.ts

author: ervcz
body:
Releases chart 3.0.0 for Nebraska 4.0.0.

Adds `config.auth.oidc.skipAudienceCheck`, and publishes `config.auth.oidc.useUserInfo`, which has been on `main` unreleased since chart 2.0.0.

Also fixes two wrong descriptions: `audience` was documented as "required for Auth0, optional for others" when it is now required for every OIDC deployment, and `rolesPath` said roles come from the id token when they come from the access token. The flag help in `backend/pkg/config/config.go` still has the id token wording and needs a separate PR.

### Breaking change

4.0.0 requires `--oidc-audience` in OIDC mode and will not start without it, see GHSA-8535-v9q5-f7qp and the [migration guide](https://github.com/flatcar/nebraska/blob/4.0.0/docs/oidc-migration-guide.md). Upgrading without setting `config.auth.oidc.audience` gives a CrashLoopBackOff rather than a readable error, so it is worth repeating in the chart release notes. `noop` and `github` modes are unaffected.

### Why caFile is removed

`--ca-file` was added in `602f75f10`, which also added the `caFile` value to the chart. That commit is on `main` but not in 4.0.0, which is cut from the 3.0.0 tag plus the security backports. So the chart would offer a value the image rejects:

```
FTL Error parsing config error="error parsing flags: flag provided but not defined: -ca-file"
```

It was never published, so nothing depends on it. Restore it alongside the next chart version bump, once an app release carries the flag.

`helm lint` is clean and every flag the chart can render exists in 4.0.0.
title: chore(helm): release chart 3.0.0 for app 4.0.0

author: richochetclementine1315
body: ## Why `pkg/config/config.go` had no test coverage. `Config.Validate()` is the last check before Nebraska starts up with a given configuration — gating packages-hosting path/URL validity, github/oidc required-field presence, and CA file existence. A regression here fails at deploy time rather than in CI, which is exactly the kind of thing worth locking down with tests. ## What this adds Table-driven tests for `Validate()`: - Flatcar-packages-hosting branch: missing path, unwritable/nonexistent path, invalid Nebraska URL, and the fully-valid case - github auth mode: all 4 required fields set (passes), all empty (fails), and missing just one field (still fails — proves the check requires all four, not just one) - oidc auth mode: same three cases as github, for the same reason - an unrecognized AuthMode (e.g. "noop"): confirmed to skip validation entirely — this is current, intended behavior (the switch has no default case), and this test exists to catch an accidental regression if that ever changes - CAFile: empty (skipped), existing (passes), nonexistent (fails) - getPotentialOrEnv(): value-present, falls-back-to-env, and neither-set cases ## What this deliberately does not cover `Parse()` is not covered. It reads `os.Args` directly and constructs a fresh `flag.FlagSet` per call; testing it would require mutating global `os.Args`, which is fragile and not good practice. > [!WARNING]
> Security release fixing [GHSA-8535-v9q5-f7qp](https://github.com/flatcar/nebraska/security/advisories/GHSA-8535-v9q5-f7qp), and a **breaking change** for OIDC deployments. Read the [migration guide](https://github.com/flatcar/nebraska/blob/4.0.0/docs/oidc-migration-guide.md) before upgrading.

### Security

- **OIDC tokens issued for other applications were accepted.** Nebraska checked a token's signature, issuer and expiry, but not its audience, so a token minted for any other application in the same realm or tenant worked against the Nebraska API. Affects 2.10.0 through 3.0.0 in OIDC mode.
- **SQL injection in the group version timeline.** The `groupID` path parameter was interpolated into three SQL statements. Any authenticated user, including a read-only one, could alter those queries. Affects 2.8.0 through 3.0.0 in **all** authentication modes.

### Breaking changes

- **`--oidc-audience` is now required** in OIDC mode, and your provider must put that value in the access token's `aud` claim. Keycloak needs an audience mapper. Without it, every request returns 401. `--oidc-skip-audience-check` restores the old behaviour for a staged migration, but leaves the vulnerability open.
- **ID tokens are no longer accepted as access tokens.** This only breaks deployments that put the API audience into ID tokens as well, which is not the Keycloak default.

`--auth-mode=noop` and `--auth-mode=github` are unaffected by both breaking changes.

### Added

- **`--oidc-use-userinfo`** reads roles from the provider's UserInfo endpoint, for providers that do not put group membership in the access token ([#1279](https://github.com/flatcar/nebraska/pull/1279)).

Full detail in [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/flatcar/nebraska/blob/4.0.0/CHANGELOG.md).

### Contributors

@ervcz, @mkilchhofer. Reported by @Moustafa-Moustafa .

### Important Notice

Version 2.13.0 was released with breaking OIDC changes that should have been v3.0.0 per [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org).

**v3.0.0 contains functionally identical code to v2.13.0** - only the version number and documentation have changed.

### What You Should Do

**If you're on v2.13.0:**
- You already completed the OIDC migration
- Updating to v3.0.0 is optional (no code/config changes)
- Recommended: Update to align with proper versioning

**If you're on v2.12.0 or earlier:**
- ⚠️ Upgrade to v3.0.0 (not v2.13.0)
- ⚠️ Follow the [OIDC Migration Guide](https://github.com/flatcar/nebraska/blob/main/docs/oidc-migration-guide.md)

**For new deployments:**
- Use v3.0.0

### Breaking Changes (Same as 2.13.0)

- **OIDC Authentication**: Complete refactor
  - Removed: `--oidc-client-secret`, `--oidc-valid-redirect-urls`, `--oidc-session-secret`, `--oidc-session-crypt-key`
  - Removed: `GET /login`, `POST /login/token`
  - Changed scopes: `openid,offline_access` → `openid,profile,email`
  - See [OIDC Migration Guide](https://github.com/flatcar/nebraska/blob/main/docs/oidc-migration-guide.md)

We apologize for this versioning mistake.

**See previous release**: https://github.com/flatcar/nebraska/releases/tag/2.13.0
**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/flatcar/nebraska/compare/2.13.0...3.0.0

**This release was incorrectly versioned.** It contains breaking changes that should have triggered a major version bump.

**Please use [v3.0.0](https://github.com/flatcar/nebraska/releases/tag/3.0.0) instead** (identical code, correct versioning).

### Breaking Changes
- **OIDC Authentication**: A complete refactor of OIDC auth that ⚠️ requires migration (see [OIDC Migration Guide](docs/oidc-migration-guide.md)) ⚠️
  - **Removed configuration options**:
    - `--oidc-client-secret` / `NEBRASKA_OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET` - OIDC now requires public client type
    - `--oidc-valid-redirect-urls` - No longer needed with direct frontend flow
    - `--oidc-session-secret` / `NEBRASKA_OIDC_SESSION_SECRET` - Backend is now stateless
    - `--oidc-session-crypt-key` / `NEBRASKA_OIDC_SESSION_CRYPT_KEY` - No server-side sessions
  - **Removed API endpoints**:
    - `GET /login` - Frontend initiates OIDC flow directly with provider
    - `POST /login/token` - Password grant type no longer supported
    - `GET /login/cb` now returns 501 for OIDC mode (GitHub mode only)
  - **Changed default scopes**: From `openid,offline_access` to `openid,profile,email`
  - **Migration requirements**:
    - OIDC provider must be reconfigured from confidential to public client type
    - CORS must be enabled for Nebraska domain on OIDC provider if it is not hosted under the same domain
    - Recommended: Enable session cookies on OIDC provider for seamless SSO re-authentication
      - Configure SSO session duration to 8-12 hours (idle timeout) and 1-7 days (maximum lifetime) based on your security requirements
      - **Keycloak**: Configure "SSO Session Max" and "SSO Session Idle Timeout" under Realm Settings → Sessions
      - **Auth0**: Configure "Maximum Session Lifetime" and "Idle Session Lifetime" under Tenant Settings → Advanced → Session Expiration
      - NOTE: Many times, these SSO session attributes are already set by default
    - When access tokens get lost after page refresh, the OIDC provider automatically re-authenticates users if SSO session is still active (no password re-entry required)
    - Recommended: Configure OIDC provider access token expiration to 1-8 hours (should be less than the SSO maximum session lifetime)
    
### Security
- **OIDC Implementation Refactor - Authorization Code Flow with PKCE** ([nebraska#642](https://github.com/flatcar/nebraska/pull/642))
  - Tokens no longer exposed in server logs or query parameters
  - Frontend handles OIDC flow directly with identity provider using PKCE (Proof Key for Code Exchange)
  - In-memory token storage prevents XSS vulnerabilities
  - Stateless backend architecture eliminates session storage related vulnerabilities

### Changed

- helm/postgresql: temporarily overwrite PostgreSQL subchart images to the Bitnami Legacy registry (`bitnamilegacy/*`) to restore Helm chart deployments after Bitnami Docker Hub deprecations. This is a short-term workaround only; Bitnami Legacy images are archived and will not receive security updates.
- backend: OIDC authentication refactored to use standard SPA authentication pattern with stateless JWT validation ([nebraska#642](https://github.com/flatcar/nebraska/pull/642))
- frontend: Implements OIDC Authorization Code Flow with PKCE directly, removing backend proxy ([nebraska#642](https://github.com/flatcar/nebraska/pull/642))
- api: Note that `oidcCookieAuth` security scheme in OpenAPI spec was never implemented and should be removed in future cleanup

author: papypom
body:
## Description

After updating Flatcar Stable from 4593.2.5 to 4757.2.0, rootless Podman could no longer pull or start the official Gotenberg image docker.io/gotenberg/gotenberg:8-chromium. The update left the rootless user namespace with only the mapping 0 500 1, despite valid /etc/subuid and /etc/subgid entries. Gotenberg uses a non-root user with UID/GID 1001, so Podman cannot unpack its image layers.

## Impact

 Gotenberg fails to start, causing PDF-generation requests from dependent applications to fail and resulting in HTTP 502 responses through Caddy.

## Environment and steps to reproduce

 1. Set-up:
     - Flatcar Container Linux Stable on Hetzner Cloud ARM64 (cax11)
     - Rootless Podman installed through the Flatcar podman system extension
     - Gotenberg managed by rootless Quadlet under user core
     - Quadlet image:
       ```text
       [Container]
       Image=docker.io/gotenberg/gotenberg:8-chromium
       AutoUpdate=registry
       ContainerName=gotenberg
       HostName=gotenberg-internal
       EnvironmentFile=%h/gotenberg.env
       PublishPort=127.0.0.1:3000:3000
       Network=caddy.network
       ```
     - /etc/subuid:
       ```text
       core:10000:65536
       ```
     - /etc/subgid:
       ```text
       core:10000:65536
       ```
     - Updated Flatcar components included:
       ```text
       podman: 5.7.1
       containers-storage: 1.59.1
       kernel: 6.12.109
       systemd: 260
       ```
     - The issue appeared after updating from Stable 4593.2.5.

 2. Task: Start the Gotenberg Quadlet service or pull the Gotenberg image.

 3. Action(s):
    a. Start the service:
    ```bash
      systemctl --user start gotenberg.service
    ```
    b. Alternatively pull the image:
    ```bash
      podman pull docker.io/gotenberg/gotenberg:8-chromium
    ```
    c. Inspect the rootless mappings:
    ```bash
      podman unshare cat /proc/self/uid_map
      podman unshare cat /proc/self/gid_map
    ```

 4. Error:

    Podman reported stale temporary layer cleanup failures such as:

    ```text
      error removing stale temp dir: unlinkat .../diff/opt/gotenberg/chromium-hyphen-data/.../hyph-gu.hyb: permission denied
    ```

    Image unpacking also failed with:

    ```text
      potentially insufficient UIDs or GIDs available in user namespace
      lchown /app: invalid argument
    ```

    The active UID/GID mappings were only:

    ```text
      0 500 1
    ```

## Expected behavior

Rootless Podman should apply the configured subordinate UID/GID ranges and successfully unpack and run the Gotenberg image, including files owned by UID/GID 1001.

## Additional information

 The official Gotenberg image intentionally creates and runs as a non-root user:

 ```dockerfile
   ARG GOTENBERG_USER_GID=1001
   ARG GOTENBERG_USER_UID=1001

   RUN groupadd --gid "$GOTENBERG_USER_GID" gotenberg \
       && useradd --uid "$GOTENBERG_USER_UID" --gid gotenberg gotenberg

   COPY --chown="$GOTENBERG_USER_UID:$GOTENBERG_USER_GID" \
     build/chromium-hyphen-data /opt/gotenberg/chromium-hyphen-data

   USER gotenberg
 ```

 The /etc/subuid and /etc/subgid configuration was correct, and running:

 ```bash
   podman system migrate
 ```

 did not restore the subordinate mappings.

 Rolling back Flatcar to the previous release restored rootless Podman functionality and allowed Gotenberg to start normally.
title: UID/GID ranges error using Podman rootless on 4757.2.0 - had to roll back to 4593.2.5

author: carlos-bilbao
body:
Flatcar's current kernel carries a major nvme-tcp bug: `nvme_tcp_init_request()` / `nvme_tcp_alloc_async_req()` use the per-queue `page_frag_cache` in a thread-unsafe way. Since v6.12 introduced async namespace scanning ([4e893ca81170](https://github.com/torvalds/linux/commit/4e893ca81170)), block devices are created in parallel and the race corrupts memory, which can cause the kernel to panic. [`main`](https://github.com/flatcar/scripts/blob/main/sdk_container/src/third_party/coreos-overlay/sys-kernel/coreos-sources/coreos-sources-6.12.105.ebuild) and the [Alpha](https://github.com/flatcar/scripts/blob/flatcar-4790/sdk_container/src/third_party/coreos-overlay/sys-kernel/coreos-sources/coreos-sources-6.12.105.ebuild)/[Beta](https://github.com/flatcar/scripts/blob/flatcar-4757/sdk_container/src/third_party/coreos-overlay/sys-kernel/coreos-sources/coreos-sources-6.12.105.ebuild)/[Stable](https://github.com/flatcar/scripts/blob/flatcar-4593/sdk_container/src/third_party/coreos-overlay/sys-kernel/coreos-sources/coreos-sources-6.12.105.ebuild) release branches all pin `coreos-sources-6.12.105`, so all are exposed.

The fix is in mainline, merged during the v7.3 merge window: [36ac05f7cfd5 ("nvme-tcp: fix usage of page_frag_cache")](https://github.com/torvalds/linux/commit/36ac05f7cfd59d90c597071304b14e98090d5dd1). I submitted the stable backports, which Sasha Levin [queued](https://lists.infradead.org/pipermail/linux-nvme/2026-August/065505.html). The 6.12.y patch is in [`stable-queue`](https://git.kernel.org/pub/scm/linux/kernel/git/stable/stable-queue.git/tree/queue-6.12/nvme-tcp-fix-usage-of-page_frag_cache.patch) and applies cleanly to `6.12.105`.

[6.12.107 was released](https://git.kernel.org/pub/scm/linux/kernel/git/stable/linux.git/tag/?h=v6.12.107) the same day the backport was queued, so the fix should land in ~6.12.108. Your automated kernel bumps will likely pick it up, but I'm filing so it's on your radar; or ideally, in case you'd take it earlier.

I'm happy to send the PR with the stable-queue patch if useful.
title: Please pick up nvme-tcp page_frag_cache fix (queued for 6.12.y) — memory corruption / kernel panics during parallel namespace scanning

author: tom-ludwig
body:
## Description

Recent Flatcar Linux releases (e.g., version `4757.2.0`) format `/etc/os-release` fields using double quotes (such as `ID="flatcar"` and `VERSION_ID="4757.2.0"`). 

When running the latest stable release of the operator (**`v0.9.0`**), `flatcar-linux-update-agent` parses these fields naively without stripping quotation marks. It then attempts to patch the Kubernetes `Node` labels with literal quotes, triggering a validation failure from the Kubernetes API server and causing the agent container to crash in a loop with exit code `255`.

Error running agent process: 
```
setting node info: setting node "<node-name>" labels: updating node "<node-name>": Node "<node-name>" is invalid: [metadata.labels: Invalid value: "\"flatcar\"": a valid label must be an empty string or consist of alphanumeric characters, '-', '_' or '.', and must start and end with an alphanumeric character (regex used for validation is '(([A-Za-z0-9][-A-Za-z0-9_.]*)?[A-Za-z0-9])?'), metadata.labels: Invalid value: "\"4757.2.0\"": ...]
```
While testing confirms this parsing issue is resolved in v0.10.0-rc2, the current stable track (v0.9.0) remains broken on all modern Flatcar nodes out of the box without manual host-side workarounds (e.g., modifying /etc/os-release).

## Impact

One node in each cluster failed to resume scheduling because the update agent could not clear its taints.
 
## Environment and steps to reproduce
- Flatcar Version: 4757.2.0
- FLUO Version: v0.9.0 (Broken), v0.10.0-rc2 (Resolved)
- Kubernetes Version: 1.36

Running `flatcar-linux-update-agent` DaemonSet (`v0.9.0`) on modern Flatcar nodes to coordinate OS updates.

a. Deployed the `flatcar-linux-update-agent` DaemonSet.
b. The first reboot completed, mounted `/etc/os-release`, and attempted to read OS metadata.
c. The agent tried to label the Kubernetes `Node` using unstripped values from `os-release`.

The agent crashes in a loop with exit code `255`:

## Expected behavior

The stable release of the operator should support modern Flatcar OS releases without requiring pre-release images (-rc*) or filesystem overrides on /etc/os-release.
Either:
- A maintenance patch (e.g., v0.9.1) is cut backporting the quote-trimming fix, or
- v0.10.0 is finalized and promoted from RC to an official GA release.
- 
## Additional information

Given that v0.9.0 was released some time ago and v0.10.0 has remained in release candidate status across few commits, what is the current roadmap and maintenance status of FLUO?

Are the maintainers looking for external contributors/maintainers to help triage issues, test PRs, or assist with release automation? Would be interested in helping maintain or contribute to the project if welcomed.
title: Latest Flatcar releases break v0.9.0 agent (quoted os-release); release status & project maintenance inquiry

body:
**Name**: app-containers/containerd
**CVEs**: [CVE-2026-53495](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-53495), [GHSA-rp3h-jf77-q9p4](https://github.com/containerd/containerd/security/advisories/GHSA-rp3h-jf77-q9p4)
**CVSSs**: TBD
**Action Needed**: update to >=2.3.5

**Summary**: 
- CVE-2026-53495: A bug in containerd's CRI ExecSync implementation allows exec probes and lifecycle hooks with background child processes to keep containerd's stdio-drain goroutines indefinitely blocked. Because the I/O drain phase lacks a default timeout or context cancellation handling, repeated ExecSync invocations (like probes) that include long-lived background processes against a container can cause containerd to leak goroutines and host memory. Over time, this resource exhaustion can cause the containerd daemon to be terminated by the OOM killer, rendering containerd unavailable until it is restarted. This issue affects containerd on Linux systems running with the CRI plugin enabled. Users not using containerd's CRI implementation or not running containers on Linux are not affected.
- GHSA-rp3h-jf77-q9p4: A vulnerability exists in containerd's layer unpack handler where the processing of certain image layers causes superlinear time complexity. During the unpack operation, specific file configurations within the layer can trigger repeated directory traversals. Consequently, pulling or importing a maliciously crafted image can result in increased unpack times and a moderate increase in CPU usage. This delays container startup, even if the compressed image layers are small. Additionally, in orchestrators like Kubernetes that apply concurrency limits to image pulls, these excessively long operations can reduce the available concurrency for other pulls, potentially delaying unrelated container deployments.

author: defo89
body:
## Description

Starting with Flatcar 4628 (Beta), `/etc` is mounted as an overlay with `noexec` via systemd-confext ([flatcar/scripts#3555](https://github.com/flatcar/scripts/pull/3555)). This breaks [Cluster API Bootstrap Provider Kubeadm (CABPK)](https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/cluster-api/tree/main/bootstrap/kubeadm) which places an executable script at `/etc/kubeadm.sh` and invokes it directly from a systemd unit.

## Impact

All Kubernetes clusters bootstrapped via CAPI Ignition format fail on Flatcar 4628+.

The CABPK Ignition template [hardcodes](https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/cluster-api/blob/main/bootstrap/kubeadm/internal/ignition/clc/clc.go#L104) the script execution.

References:
- [`ExecStart=/etc/kubeadm.sh` (line 104)](https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/cluster-api/blob/main/bootstrap/kubeadm/internal/ignition/clc/clc.go#L104)
- [`path: /etc/kubeadm.sh` (line 210)](https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/cluster-api/blob/main/bootstrap/kubeadm/internal/ignition/clc/clc.go#L210)
- [`path: /etc/kubeadm.yml` (line 226)](https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/cluster-api/blob/main/bootstrap/kubeadm/internal/ignition/clc/clc.go#L226)

## Environment and steps to reproduce

- Flatcar: 4628.1.2 (Beta)
- Previous working: 4593.2.1 (Stable)
- CAPI: v1.9+ with Ignition bootstrap format

1. Provision a node with Flatcar 4628.1.2 using CAPI with Ignition bootstrap format
2. `kubeadm.service` fails with:

```bash
 # journalctl -u kubeadm.service
Jun 09 14:02:59 node01-001 systemd[1]: Starting kubeadm.service - kubeadm...
Jun 09 14:02:59 node01-001 (beadm.sh)[5827]: kubeadm.service: Unable to locate executable '/etc/kubeadm.sh': Permission denied
Jun 09 14:02:59 node01-001 (beadm.sh)[5827]: kubeadm.service: Failed at step EXEC spawning /etc/kubeadm.sh: Permission denied
Jun 09 14:02:59 node01-001 systemd[1]: kubeadm.service: Main process exited, code=exited, status=203/EXEC
Jun 09 14:02:59 node01-001 systemd[1]: kubeadm.service: Failed with result 'exit-code'.
Jun 09 14:02:59 node01-001 systemd[1]: Failed to start kubeadm.service - kubeadm.

 node01-001 ~ # /etc/kubeadm.sh
 -bash: /etc/kubeadm.sh: Permission denied

 node01-001 ~ # findmnt /etc
 TARGET SOURCE  FSTYPE  OPTIONS
 /etc   confext overlay rw,nosuid,nodev,noexec,noatime,seclabel,...
```

## Expected behavior

CAPI nodes can join the cluster.

## Additional information

I am not sure what's the most optimal fix and whether `noexec` should be reverted as I fully acknowledge the intend of the behaviour.

The Issue is that CABPK does not offer an API to change kubeadm script file location.
title: `/etc` mounted with `noexec` (confext overlay) breaks Cluster API kubeadm bootstrap

**CVEs**: [CVE-2026-5435](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-5435), [CVE-2026-5450](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-5450), [CVE-2026-5928](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-5928), [CVE-2026-6238](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-6238), [CVE-2026-6368](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-6368), [CVE-2026-6791](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-6791), [CVE-2026-18374](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-18374), [CVE-2026-89092](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-89092)
**CVSSs**: 7.3, 9.8, 7.5, 6.5, 2.1, 6.6, 4.9, 4.2
**Action Needed**:
  * CVE-2026-{5435,5450,5928,6238,6368,6791}: update to >= 2.44
  * CVE-2026-18374, CVE-2026-89092: update to >= 2.45

**Summary**:
  * CVE-2026-5435: The deprecated functions ns_printrrf, ns_printrr and fp_nquery in the GNU C Library version 2.2 and newer fail to enforce the caller-supplied buffer length, and can result in an out-of-bounds write when printing TSIG records.
    * https://lwn.net/Articles/1071079/
  * CVE-2026-5450: Calling the scanf family of functions with a %mc (malloc'd character match) in the GNU C Library version 2.7 to version 2.43 with a format width specifier with an explicit width greater than 1024 could result in a one byte heap buffer overflow.
    * https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=2459853
  * CVE-2026-5928: Calling the ungetwc function on a FILE stream with wide characters encoded in a character set that has overlaps between its single byte and multi-byte character encodings, in the GNU C Library version 2.43 or earlier, may result in an attempt to read bytes before an allocated buffer, potentially resulting in unintentional disclosure of neighboring data in the heap, or a program crash. A bug in the wide character pushback implementation (_IO_wdefault_pbackfail in libio/wgenops.c) causes ungetwc() to operate on the regular character buffer (fp->_IO_read_ptr) instead of the actual wide-stream read pointer (fp->_wide_data->_IO_read_ptr). The program crash may happen in cases where fp->_IO_read_ptr is not initialized and hence points to NULL. The buffer under-read requires a special situation where the input character encoding is such that there are overlaps between single byte representations and multibyte representations in that encoding, resulting in spurious matches. The spurious match case is not possible in the standard Unicode character sets.
    * https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=2459854
  * CVE-2026-6238: The deprecated functions ns_printrrf, ns_printrr and fp_nquery in the GNU C Library version 2.2 and newer fail to validate the RDATA content against the RDATA length in a DNS response when processing LOC, CERT, TKEY or TSIG records, which may allow an attacker to craft a DNS response, causing a target application to crash or read uninitialized memory. These functions are for application debugging only and hence not in the path of code executed by the DNS resolver. Further, they have been deprecated since version 2.34 and should not be used by any new applications. Applications should consider porting away from these interfaces since they may be removed in future versions.
    * https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=2463539
  * CVE-2026-6368: Calling wordexp with WRDE_APPEND in the GNU C Library version 2.0 to version 2.43 can cause the interface to return invalid memory in the we_wordv member, which on subsequent calls to wordfree may abort the process.
  * CVE-2026-6791: When expanding paths that begin with a tilde (~) followed by a username, the internal parse_tilde function extracts the username to determine the user's home directory. The implementation allocates memory for this username directly on the stack using the strndupa macro. Because the size of this allocation was determined by the length of the user-supplied input without any bounds checks, passing an excessively long username e.g. thousands of characters, forces the thread to exhaust its stack space. Thus if an application passes untrusted, attacker-controlled input to the wordexp function, an attacker can trigger a stack clash.
  * CVE-2026-18374: Passing an effectively empty string to the `,ccs=` syntax extension of the mode argument in the `fopen` function in the GNU C Library version 2.45 or earlier may result in a heap buffer overflow when the mode string input to the function is attacker controlled. This usage pattern is not seen in applications in common GNU/Linux distributions and applications that process user-supplied values for `ccs` should not pass them through without validation.
    * https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=2525256
  * CVE-2026-89092: The nscd service in the GNU C Library 2.3.4 onwards may crash due to a stack overflow when a malicious DNS server returns too large a response for a DNS query, resulting in degraded DNS resolution for the system. Exploitation of this bug needs a system that has nscd enabled and using an untrusted DNS server for name resolution, with the compromised DNS server being capable of processing records large enough to result in a stack overflow in an nscd thread stack.  During experimentation, bind 9 was unable to handle large records, but that could change in future or with a different name server.  In typical installations, nscd is executed in an isolated context as its own user without a shell, due to which any compromise of that service is isolated. There is a remote possibility of nscd cache corruption if an attacker manages to get the stack pointer into a desired point in the heap, potentially resulting in other caches in nscd being overwritten with corrupt data through the stack overflow, until the buggy code path eventually results in a crash. Finally, a crash in nscd may result in performance degradation when resolving names, but it does not result in a denial of service.
    * https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=2531725

**Name**: dev-libs/libpcre2
**CVEs**: [CVE-2026-86145](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-86145), [CVE-2026-89156](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-89156), [CVE-2026-89161](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-89161), [GHSA-9qww-pwc4-77qq](https://github.com/PCRE2Project/pcre2/security/advisories/GHSA-9qww-pwc4-77qq), [GHSA-q7rw-r7qq-2hx6](https://github.com/PCRE2Project/pcre2/security/advisories/GHSA-q7rw-r7qq-2hx6)
**CVSSs**: 8.2, 7.4, 2.9, 3.7, 2.9
**Action Needed**: update to >= 10.48

**Summary**:
  * CVE-2026-86145: PCRE2 before 10.48 allows a pcre2_dfa_match out-of-bounds write because reuse of a cached workspace block, in a recursive DFA matching workspace, lacks a size check (even though a newly allocated block, for the same purpose, does have a size check). This outcome requires an attacker-controlled regular expression, or a recursive pattern in conjunction with a small heap limit (this can be set through the API).
  * CVE-2026-89156: PCRE2 before 10.48 has a pcre2_match out-of-bounds read after a JIT fallback when an attacker can provide invalid UTF data.
    * https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=2531743
  * CVE-2026-89161: In PCRE2 before 10.48, pcre2_jit_match mishandles a previously copied subject being passed in as a context. An incorrect free operation can occur.
    * https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=2531747
  * GHSA-9qww-pwc4-77qq: The PCRE2 interpreter can read before the start of an invalid UTF subject while performing certain backward character scans. This occurs because two paths use their bound as the beginning of the complete subject instead of the beginning of the region that has been validated as UTF.
  * GHSA-q7rw-r7qq-2hx6: A compiled and serialized regular expression may contain two bytes of uninitialized data from previous memory allocations.

author: simar0at
body:
## Current situation

QEMU provides a virtual watchdog device in its q35 machine. It is a (variant of the ?) `iTCO_wdt`. There are however three modules (`mfd_core`, `intel_pmc_bxt`, `lpc_ich`) missing in sys-kernel/coreos-modules that are needed beside the `iTCO_*` modules.

## Impact

Although the `iTCO_wdt` module is available, the only watchdog option in QEMU based runtime environments is `softdog`.

## Ideal future situation

Build the three modules `mfd_core`, `intel_pmc_bxt` and `lpc_ich` needed for the q35 based virtual watchdog.

## Implementation options

```patch
diff --git a/sdk_container/src/third_party/coreos-overlay/sys-kernel/coreos-modules/files/amd64_defconfig-6.12 b/sdk_container/src/third_party/coreos-overlay/sys-kernel/coreos-modules/files/amd64_defconfig-6.12
index a6eb3aeffc..1322e2c074 100644
--- a/sdk_container/src/third_party/coreos-overlay/sys-kernel/coreos-modules/files/amd64_defconfig-6.12
+++ b/sdk_container/src/third_party/coreos-overlay/sys-kernel/coreos-modules/files/amd64_defconfig-6.12
@@ -76,8 +76,10 @@ CONFIG_KPROBES_ON_FTRACE=y
 CONFIG_KVM=m
 CONFIG_KVM_AMD=m
 CONFIG_KVM_INTEL=m
+CONFIG_LPC_ICH=m
 CONFIG_MEMORY_FAILURE=y
 CONFIG_MEM_SOFT_DIRTY=y
+CONFIG_MFD_INTEL_PMC_BXT=m
 CONFIG_MMC_SDHCI_ACPI=m
 # CONFIG_MOUSE_PS2_LIFEBOOK is not set
 CONFIG_MTRR_SANITIZER_ENABLE_DEFAULT=1
```
title: [RFE] The QEMU q35 virtual watchdog should be available in flatcar linux

**Name**: app-arch/xz-utils
**CVEs**: [GHSA-5qpq-xqfv-j9pg](https://github.com/tukaani-project/xz/security/advisories/GHSA-5qpq-xqfv-j9pg)
**CVSSs**: n/a
**Action Needed**: update to >= 5.8.4

**Summary**:

In XZ Utils 5.8.3 and older, an invalid memory write can occur in decoders that are initialized using the following functions:

  * lzma_alone_decoder (decodes .lzma files)
  * lzma_lzip_decoder (decodes .lz files)
  * lzma_auto_decoder (when decoding .lzma or .lz files)
  * lzma_microlzma_decoder (decodes MicroLZMA format)

Required steps:

  1. A lzma_stream is initialized using one of the above functions.
  1. A file is decoded at least partially.
  1. The same lzma_stream is reinitialized using the same function.
  1. Another file is decoded but memory allocation fails with LZMA_MEM_ERROR. (LZMA_MEMLIMIT_ERROR doesn't cause this.)
  1. The same lzma_stream is reinitialized again using the same function.
  1. A file is decoded. It must specify the same dictionary size as the file in step 2.

Decoders for the .xz format and raw streams aren't affected.

The issue has been fixed in XZ Utils 5.8.4 and in the Git repository branch v5.8. The fix is also in the Git repository branches v5.6, v5.4, and v5.2, but no new releases will be made from these old branches.

**Name**: net-libs/libpcap
**CVEs**: [CVE-2026-0799](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-0799), [CVE-2026-18238](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-18238), [CVE-2026-18313](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-18313), [CVE-2026-31911](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-31911), [CVE-2026-31912](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-31912), [CVE-2026-6244](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-6244), [CVE-2026-6554](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-6554)
**CVSSs**: 8.7, 5.0, 4.3, 5.5, 5.5, 5.5, 5.5
**Action Needed**: update to >= 1.10.7

**Summary**:
  * CVE-2026-0799: In BPF instructions that load/store a value from/to a scratch memory register the register index is an unsigned 32-bit integer and must not exceed 15, but libpcap BPF interpreter does not validate the value. In particular uncommon use cases a crafted filter program can cause the interpreter to try reading and writing the OS process memory in the 16GiB starting at the current stack frame on 64-bit architectures and in the entire address space on 32-bit architectures.
  * CVE-2026-18238: The rpcap client code that processes a RPCAP_MSG_PACKET message received from the server incorrectly validates its headers. A malicious server can send a crafted message and cause the client to treat up to 20 bytes of the client process memory beyond the end of the buffer as if it was a part of the captured packet.
  * CVE-2026-18313: pcapd can allocate up to 65536 bytes per each RPCAP_MSG_UPDATEFILTER_REQ or RPCAP_MSG_STARTCAP_REQ message received from the client, but it never frees the memory, so it leaks memory even under normal use. A malicious client can cause the server to leak memory substantially faster.
  * CVE-2026-31911: libpcap BPF interpreter calls abort() if it encounters a BPF instruction that has an invalid opcode. In particular uncommon use cases a crafted filter program can terminate the OS process.
  * CVE-2026-31912: libpcap BPF interpreter detects neither reaching the end of the filter program buffer due to lack of a return instruction nor executing a jump instruction with an offset that translates to a pointer outside of the buffer. In particular uncommon use cases a crafted filter program can cause the interpreter to try reading the OS process memory in the 32GiB around the buffer on 64-bit architectures and in the entire address space on 32-bit architectures.
  * CVE-2026-6244: libpcap BPF interpreter for the 'div #k' and 'mod #k' ALU instructions does not check whether the immediate value is zero. In particular uncommon use cases a crafted filter program can cause a division by zero.
  * CVE-2026-6554: libpcap BPF interpreter treats the offset in the 'ja L' BPF instruction as a signed integer to implement looping via backward jumps, but it does not limit the number of loop iterations. In particular uncommon use cases a crafted filter program can cause the interpreter to loop infinitely.
